transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alicia (CopperLode Head of AI), Marcus (SRE), Devon (Finance)

Summary:
Quick Q2 health check focused on unexpected cost variance in March, discussion of Dedicated capacity for peak-hour risk mitigation, validation of latency targets (95th pctl), and next steps for pilot and pricing. Action items assigned and follow-ups scheduled.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh, appreciate the time. We're here for the Q2 health and budget sync for CopperLode, go over March variance and plan for the upcoming peak in June.
00:14 Alicia: Thanks Jordan. Quick heads up — Devon had to hop on late so he might be a bit quiet, but Marcus will covers the infra details.
00:22 Marcus: Yep, hey all. We saw a spike mid-March on inference calls, largely due to a new scoring route.
00:35 Priya: I pulled the usage breakdown — the majority of tokens were from the scoring endpoint with longer sequence lengths, so cost per call increased. We also noticed KV cache hit rates were lower at peak which drove more compute.
00:50 Devon: Right, and our finance team flagged a 37% overrun vs forecast for March, hence this meeting.
01:05 Jordan: Got it. To orient — quick reminder: you can use Redwood Hosted API for elastic consumption, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, or Redwood Private if you need V P C/on-prem. Today we'll focus on Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs because residency and SOC2 are already satisfied.
01:28 Alicia: Can you run through the committed pricing again? The sheet we have seems different from what we talked about in the pilot.
01:35 Jordan: Sure — I'll send the latest committed-use pricing after the call. Short version: committed Reserved capacity discounts kick in at monthly commit levels and you get better unit economics on token spend compared to pure hosted. We'll share a comparison spreadsheet.
01:53 Marcus: Two operational questions: 1) If we go Dedicated, do we still get automatic fallback to Hosted during capacity blips? 2) How are KV caches shared or isolated across tenants?
02:08 Priya: For 1, yes — there is a smart routing policy. During a Dedicated outage or capacity depletion, requests can fall back to compatible Hosted model variants automatically. For 2, Dedicated can be configured with isolated KV caches per tenant; Hosted uses cluster-level caching with namespace isolation but sometimes hit rate behavior differs.
02:33 Marcus: Okay, good. The fallback behavior is critical because we run a customer-facing scoring pipeline with 200ms P95 target.
02:45 Priya: Right, so we should run a 95th percentile latency benchmark with your real payloads. That will show the P95 under steady-state and burst. I can do that — will need the traffic profile and sequence length distribution.
03:03 Alicia: We'll share the profiles. A quick question about quantization: we've heard Redwood has some recommended quantization profiles that lower cost but might affect quality — what's your advice?
03:18 Priya: We recommend model-quantization profiles per workload. For retrieval and classification tasks the 4-bit quantization yields minimal quality drop, but for generation-heavy, long-form outputs you might prefer fp16 or q8 to preserve quality. Redwood Optimize will propose settings, but we'll validate on your evals.
03:38 Devon: On costs — can you explain the March variance? We had some optimistic assumptions about average tokens per call.
03:46 Priya: The main driver was sequence tail: a small percentage of calls had tokens 3-5x average because we didn't cap or compress at the client side. Also lower cache hits meant more tokens actually processed by the runtime.
03:59 Jordan: Another leaky area is continuous batching configuration. If batching window is too small under low load you pay more per-token. We can provide tuning suggestions that often reduce per-token unit costs by 10-25% depending on workload.
04:18 Marcus: Is that an automated tuning or will it need SE time?
04:22 Priya: There are both: Optimize provides suggestions and Redwood SEs can help implement server-side policies. For Dedicated we can also tweak kernel selection and batching thresholds.
04:35 Alicia: On SLA — we get the standard uptime SLO, but our legal team wants clarity on latency SLOs for the scoring endpoint. Is there an SLA addendum for latency?
04:47 Jordan: Latency SLOs are available on the Dedicated contracts as part of higher-tier SLAs. We'll map expected P95 numbers — but as Priya said, we'll need to run the benchmark to validate the numbers under your real traffic.
05:03 Devon: If we move to Dedicated, what's the expected procurement lead time? We may need a month to modify forecasts and get approvals.
05:12 Jordan: Typical lead time for Dedicated capacity is 4-8 weeks depending on region and GPU availability; we can provision burst capacity earlier if you need immediate headroom.
05:25 Marcus: Any hardware vendor constraints? We're sensitive to specific kernel optimizations for some models.
05:30 Priya: We work with multiple backends and pick kernels per model and hardware. If you have preferred hardware (e.g., A100 vs H100 vs Lambda hardware), tell us and we'll align. Note: kernel-level tuning can change latency characteristics.
05:50 Alicia: Security — legal asked for KMS integration and audit logs. Do you support customer-managed keys?
05:56 Jordan: Yes — Redwood Private and Dedicated both support customer K M S integrations and centralized audit logs. We'll share the compliance pack with SOC2/ISO artifacts.
06:10 Alicia: Great, please send that. Also, data residency — we need EU-only residency for a subset of PII. Can you support per-route residency?
06:20 Priya: Yes, routing policies can pin routes to region-specific pools; we also support V P C connectors for Private deployments to satisfy residency and network controls.
06:33 Marcus: Back to cost — any quick levers we can turn today to arrest overspend before Q2?
06:40 Jordan: Short term: 1) cap max tokens per call at the client side, 2) enable prefix caching for common prompts, 3) apply suggested quantization on lower-risk routes, 4) tune batching windows. We can push a ticket with SE priorities.
06:58 Devon: Okay — Finance would like to see an updated 90-day forecast if we adopt a committed plan vs staying hosted.
07:05 Jordan: We'll produce a three-scenario forecast: stay-hosted baseline, committed Dedicated, and hybrid (Hosted + Dedicated reserved for peak). We'll include unit economics and break-even point.
07:17 Alicia: Timeline — we'd like the Dedicated evaluation before the June traffic increase. Can you commit to benchmarks and pricing by end of April?
07:26 Jordan: Yes — action items to get that to you. Priya will run the benchmarks and I will send pricing.

-- mid call, deeper technical dive --
15:05 Priya: (to Marcus) can you confirm average and 95th percentile sequence lengths and distribution? That will determine kernel pathing and batching behavior.
15:16 Marcus: Average is about 120 tokens but the tail goes to 900 on some scoring jobs — those are the ones spiking cost.
15:27 Priya: That explains it. For tails like that we recommend aggressive prefix/KV caching and if it's possible to shorten or truncate non-critical context.
15:36 Marcus: There's also a route that calls a re-ranker which triggers multiple model calls per request. That multiplies cost.
15:45 Priya: Reranking is expensive — options are to do a lighter-weight candidate filter before hitting the big model, or serve the re-ranker on Dedicated with better cache locality.
15:58 Devon: From finance, can you show the sensitivity if we reduce tail calls by 50%?
16:05 Jordan: We'll include that scenario in the forecast — early back-of-envelope says 20-30% savings on total spend if you can limit tail frequency.

-- procurement notes and risks --
28:40 Alicia: Our procurement is also asking about vendor lock-in and portability. If we take Dedicated, how hard is it to move workloads later?
28:52 Jordan: We try to avoid lock-in: you can pin model versions and export model artifacts; standard APIs persist. However Dedicated optimizations (quantization, kernel tuning) may need retuning on a new provider. We'll provide runbooks for migrations.
29:10 Marcus: Are there egress costs if we do hybrid routing to a different region for overflow?
29:16 Priya: Yes, egress/network costs can apply and we'll call that out explicitly in the pricing scenarios.

-- recap and next steps --
48:30 Jordan: Recap: 1) Jordan send pricing and compliance pack by Friday. 2) Priya run P95 latency benchmarks and share results. 3) Marcus provide traffic profiles. 4) Alicia confirm compliance and residency requirements. 5) Redwood produce three-scenario forecast. Is everyone aligned?
48:52 Alicia: Yes. 48:54 Devon: Sounds good.
49:01 Marcus: One more ask — can you include a quick guide for client-side token caps and prompt compression best practices?
49:09 Priya: We'll include a one-page best-practices doc with the benchmark results.
49:18 Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for a pilot kick-off and the next check-in in two weeks after the benchmark.
49:29 Alicia: Appreciate it. Thanks everyone.
49:33 Jordan: Thanks all, talk soon.

Questions noted:
- Do we have a latency SLA addendum for Dedicated? (Answer: yes, with validated benchmarks)
- Can we do per-route residency? (Answer: yes, via routing policies and Private/VPC)

End of transcript.
